Name: Optimus Prime
Alternate Mode: White Freightliner Cabover Engine Tractor Trailer FLA 8664T
Notes: White Freightliner Cabover Engine Tractor Trailer FLA 8664T. The early versions were near identical to the Diaclone Battle Convoy & came with metal plates in the trailer rather than stickers and it also came with  'swollen' accessories and a grey Roller. The early box also featured an error; the radar dish is visible under the box art and has not been cropped from the underside of the box. Later releases had the standard thinner gun and blue Roller and stickers in the trailer instead of metal plates.

Name: Bluestreak
Notes: Silver Nissan Fairlady 280Z-T. Although the box art and catalogues depict a "blue" Bluesteak, this was not released in the Transformers line.

Name: Hound
Notes: Near identical to the original Diaclone version

Name: Ironhide
Notes: Red Cherry Vannette, this colour was unreleased in the Japanese Diaclone series but did appear in GiGs Trasformer series. Ironhide was also unreleased in Japan. As Ironhide did not have a head, there was a face sticker included to attach to the drivers seat.

Name: Jazz
Notes: Martini (deliberately misspelt Martinii) team racing livery. Takara had previously released a Cosmo Porsche in 1977 under the Microman Command line, these came in red, blue and white.

Name: Mirage
Notes: Citanes is a reworded "Gitanes" which are a brand of French cigarettes

Name: Prowl
Notes: Based on the Nissan Fairlady Z (S130), marketed internationally as the Datsun 280ZX. The livery is based on a Japanese Aichi Prefecture Highway Patrol cruiser rather than an American police car, despite featuring English "POLICE" and "HIGHWAY PATROL" door decals. The door shields originally retained Japanese characters (Keishicho) in Diaclone, which were altered to a stylized crest for Transformers. Early G1 releases retain the "Datsun" branding stamped into the rear bumper chrome and red plastic light bar brackets, later simplified to clear/red plastic.

Name: Ratchet
Notes: Ratchet was initially supposed to be a female character, the name is based on "Nurse Rached" from "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest". The early versions of Ratchet feature a red cross on the van roof which is also depicted on the box art. This was later removed, potentially at the Red Cross' (international humanitarian aid group) as they are protective of their brand. As Ratchet did not have a head, there was a face sticker included to attach to the drivers seat.

Name: Sideswipe
Notes: Red Lamborghini Countach LP500S. Due to the similarities with Sunstreaker, their profiles were accidentlly switched.

Name: Skids
Notes: Honda City Turbo. Skids was released late 1984 although he was not advertised with the 1984 Autobot cars. There are two different versions of the box, one with a 1984 date and the other with a 1985 date and amended product code. Takara's 2002 reissue of Skids confirms the 1984 release date.

Name: Sunstreaker
Notes: Lamborghini Countach LP500S based on Takaras "Cosmo Countach" from 1977 Microman Command. Due to the similarities with Sideswipe, their profiles were accidentlly switched.

Name: Trailbreaker
Notes: Based on a third-generation 1978–1983 Toyota Hilux 4WD short-bed pickup truck fitted with a camper shell. Originating as Diaclone Car Robot No. 8, the real-world vehicle was famous for popularizing compact 4x4 off-roading globally. The toy features realistic yellow, orange, and red body striping typical of late 1970s custom Toyota trim packages, along with "4WD" factory branding molded into the front grille and tailgate.

Name: Wheeljack
Notes: Based on the Lancia Stratos which raced in the 1976 FIA Group 5. The livery was initially the red Marlboro (cigarette company). The  remaing #598 car (#599 was written off in the race) was repainted in the green Alitalia livery, an Itallian airline company, spelt "Alitalla" on the toy and numbered 539. The #539 car was driven to victory in the Giro D'Italia in 1977

Name: Brawn
Notes: Dark green Jeep Wrangler, originally from Takaras Micro Change line. There is evidence to suggest Gears (along with Brawn, Windcharger & Huffer) came from the unreleased Knickerbocker "Mysterians" series and was named Jeepar. There is an "M" moulded on Brawn's bonnet which you could be excused for thinking it stands for "Micro Change" but this same stylised "M" appears on the "Mysterian" figures released by Marchon inc in 1984. Gears was unreleased in Japan.

Name: Bumblebee
Notes: Based on a Choro-Q (aka Penny Racer) Volkswagen Type-1 (aka VW Beetle), originally from Takaras Micro Change line. A red version was also available in order to bulk up the toy line. The red version was also available in 1985.

Name: Cliffjumper
Notes: Based on a Choro-Q (aka Penny Racer) Porsche 924 Turbo, originally from Takaras Micro Change line. A yellow version was also available in order to bulk up the toy line. The yellow version was also available in 1985.

Name: Gears
Notes: Red & Blue Pick-Up Truck, originally from Takaras Micro Change line. There is evidence to suggest Gears (along with Brawn, Windcharger & Huffer) came from the unreleased Knickerbocker "Mysterians" series and was named Blazar. There is an "M" moulded on Gears bonnet which you could be excused for thinking it stands for "Micro Change" but this same stylised "M" appears on the "Mysterian" figures released by Marchon inc in 1984. Gears was unreleased in Japan.

Name: Huffer
Notes: Orange Semi-Cab, originally from Takaras Micro Change line. There is evidence to suggest Huffer (along with Brawn, Windcharger & Gears) came from the unreleased Knickerbocker "Mysterians" series and was named Truckar. There is an "M" moulded on Huffers cab door which you could be excused for thinking it stands for "Micro Change" but this same stylised "M" appears on the "Mysterian" figures released by Marchon inc in 1984.

Name: Windcharger
Notes: Red Pontiac Firebird, originally from Takaras Micro Change line. There is evidence to suggest Windcharger (along with Brawn, Huffer & Gears) came from the unreleased Knickerbocker "Mysterians" series and was named Speedar.

Name: Bumper
Notes: Based on a Choro-Q (aka Penny Racer) Mazda Familia XG1500. Not an official Transformer release, possibly used to bulk up the initial toy line as with the yellow Cliffjumper and red Bumblebee. Said to have been sold on both Cliffjumper or Bumblebee card but the only carded versions found have only been on Cliffjumpers backing card.

Notes: Mail Away. Triple Changer - car mode, attack mode and robot mode. The Omnibots did not come with Tech Specs however it was later found that writer Bob Budiansky had written offical bios that were never used. Mail order through pamphlets "Reinforcements From Cybertron!" (offer ended 30/06/1985)

Notes: Mail Away. Autobot logo watch. The logo splits in half to reveal the time. Mail order through pamphlets "Reinforcements From Cybertron!" (offer ended 30/06/1985)

Name: Megatron
Notes: Chromed Walther P-38 pistol with extensions. Based on the gun in the TV Show "The Man From U.N.C.L.E". Early versions maintained the spring firing mechanism but this was removed for later releases. Came with a stock, silencer, scope and infrared laser. The stock, scope and silencer have various combinations.

Name: Soundwave
Notes: "Soundwave And Condor Cassette Buzzsaw". Soundwave comes packaged with Buzzsaw who transforms into a Microcassette which fits inside Soundwave. Soundwaves weapons double as AA batteries which can fit in his back when the belt clip is removed.

Name: Buzzsaw
Notes: "Soundwave And Condor Cassette Buzzsaw". Soundwave comes packaged with Buzzsaw who transforms into a Microcassette which fits inside Soundwave. Buzzsaw is a gold repaint on Laserbeak, this colour scheme was only released in the Transformers series and did not appear in the original Micro Change line.

Name: Laserbeak
Notes: Microcassette 2-Pack. Laserbeak transforms into a red Condor

Name: Rumble
Notes: Microcassette 2-Pack. Unlike the cartoon, the red cassette is Rumble. In the Japanese dub this mistake was corrected and the red cassette was renamed Rumble.

Name: Ravage
Notes: Microcassette 2-Pack. Ravage transforms into a black jaguar.

Name: Frenzy
Notes: Microcassette 2-Pack. Unlike the cartoon, the blue cassette is Frenzy. In the Japanese dub this mistake as corrected and the blue cassette was renamed Frenzy.

Name: Skywarp
Notes: The black and purple colours are new to the Transformers series and did not appear in the earlier Diaclone line. The tech spec number values were mixed up with Starscream on the box hence why Skywarps rank is 9

Name: Starscream
Notes: Red & grey jet. The tech spec number values were mixed up with Skywarp on the box, hence Starscreams rank of 5.

Name: Thundercracker
Notes: Based on the McDonnell Douglas F-15C Eagle air superiority fighter. Originating from Takara's 1983 Diaclone line as the "Jet Robo F-15 Eagle Acrobat Type", the blue metallic coloration was an official acrobatic team variant rather than a real-world military camouflage scheme. The toy retains the opening cockpit canopy designed to seat a tiny Diaclone magnetic pilot figure. Early 1984 releases featured a sharp, hard-plastic nosecone and unnumbered accessory sprues before being updated with a rounded rubber safety tip and modified mold stamps.

Name: Omega Supreme
Notes: Defence Base & Tank. This is an electronic figure - robot could walk and tank could go round the track. The robot mode head module also flashes a red light. Redeco of Mechabot-1 from Toybox. Omega Sureme was unreleased in the UK due to the licensing of the mould to Grandstand for their Convertors range of toys. Unreleased in Japan

Name: Perceptor
Notes: Transforms into a working microscope and a tank.

Name: Jetfire
Notes: Macross Valkryie. Early releases had the Macross emblem on the wing. Hasbro acquired the rights from Takatoku Toys, designed by Shoji Kawamori. The designs were bought by Bandai forcing Hasbro to dramatically alter Jetfires cartoon model and rename the characer as Skyfire. Jetfire is a redeco of the 1983 1/55 VF-1S Super Valkyrie. Jetfire comes with armour which can attach to the jet mode and robot mode. Also features a GERWALK mode (Ground Effective Reinforcement of Winged Armament with Locomotive Knee-joint). Unreleased in Japan

Name: Blaster
Notes: Red & grey portable stereo. Early versions came with a removable cover on the reverse of the figure whch was a left over from the original Microchange mould. Blaster features "working" buttons under the opening cassette door, after pressing the play button youcan press stop to spring it back up and the eject button opens the cassette door. Sometimes the eject button won't work but this is easily fixable.

Name: Beachcomber
Notes: Based on a Chenowth Navy Fast Attack Vehicle (FAV) / DPV (Desert Patrol Vehicle), a lightweight military dune buggy used by US Special Forces. Designed specifically for the 1985 Minibot assortment rather than repurposed from Micro Change, Beachcomber features a real rubber rear spare tire and a die-cast metal chest panel. His roll cage assembly is made of flexible PVC plastic to prevent snapping.

Name: Cosmos
Notes: Based on an Adamski-style Flying Saucer, specifically inspired by the saucer designs popularized by UFO contactee George Adamski in the 1950s (notably the 1952 "Venusian Scout Ship" photos). Unlike the 1984 Minibots derived from Takara's Micro Change line, Cosmos was an original Hasbro/Takara creation designed specifically for Transformers.

Name: Powerglide
Notes: Based on the Fairchild Republic A-10 Thunderbolt II attack aircraft, commonly known as the "Warthog". To fit the small Minibot scale, the aircraft's proportions were heavily stylized with oversized rear turbofan engines and stubby wings.

Name: Seaspray
Notes: Based on a hovercraft, loosely modeled after the SR.N4 Mountbatten-class passenger hovercraft that operated across the English Channel. Another original Transformers design not originating from Micro Change, Seaspray features dual rear thruster turbines on swivel joints that rotate downward to act as heels in robot mode.

Name: Warpath
Notes: General Motors M551 Sheridan AR/AAV. Designed specifically for the 1985 Minibot line, Warpath features a robot chest dominated by his vehicle mode's main tank turret and gun barrel. His tank treads are molded, non-functional plastic, relying on small hidden wheels underneath the chassis for rolling movement.

Name: Topspin
Notes: Tank. Early versions had D.A.R on the wing stickers. Features a pull-back motor which when pulled back in vehicle mode and let go, the vehicle would dash forwards and then the figure would "jump" instantly transforming to a robot.

Name: Twin Twist

Name: Bombshell
Notes: Based on a Japanese rhinoceros beetle (Allomyrina dichotoma). Originating from Takara's 1983 Diaclone line as the "Insecter Robo Kabutron", the original toy featured an orange torso canopy that opened to seat a tiny magnetic pilot figure—a leftover cavity retained in the Transformers release behind his head/cerebral shell. His head-mounted head-canon weapon original fired small plastic missiles in Japan, but was neutered with a non-firing spring mechanism for Western safety regulations.

Name: Kickback
Notes: Based on a grasshopper (Caelifera). Released in Japan as the Diaclone "Insecter Robo Batta-Man", Kickback was designed with chromed wings and die-cast metal in his waist and internal joints. Like his wave-mates, the translucent yellow chest panel originally functioned as a cockpit cover for a pilot figure.

Name: Shrapnel
Notes: Based on a stag beetle (Lucanidae). Derived from the Diaclone "Insecter Robo Kuwagaten", his signature large chrome pincer mandibles were designed to double as a weapon mount in beetle mode and shoulder antennae/pincers in robot mode. Early production runs featured sharp points on his chrome mandibles and gun accessories, which were later remolded with blunted tips for child safety.

Name: Astrotrain
Alternate Mode: C62 Steam Locomotive / Space Shuttle Orbiter
Notes: Transforms from robot to train and space shuttle. Astrotrain was a design that was unreleased from Takaras Diaclone series. Early prototypes of Astrotrain featured a dark grey shuttle and a purple train. The colours were altered before its release yet the box art and cartoon retained the colour pallette.

Name: Convoy
Alternate Mode: White Freightliner Cabover Engine Tractor Trailer FLA 8664T
Notes: Released June 1985. The Japanese release has four versions. The first version is an easy spot because there is no barcode on the rear of the box (pictured above). This version comes with a silver Buggy (Roller) without the 2 rear pegs, bloated fists and gun, and the silver missiles. The second version comes with a silver Buggy (Roller) without the 2 rear pegs, bloated fists and gun, and the silver missiles and the trailer features the metal plates. The rear of the box features the barcode. The third version has Buggy (Roller) without the 2 pegs moulded on the rear as per the original Diaclone release, the blue plastic in the trailer and on Buggy is also dark blue; it also includes the "bloated" fists and gun and it also comes with silver missiles.  The fourth version is similar to Hasbro's release with the pegs included with Buggy and the standard gun and fists. The powerful launcher within the trailer in all versions is retained. Despite these differences from Hasbro's version, the box photography depicts the Joustra / Hasbro's pre-rub sign Optimus Prime. Interestingly the box art is different from Hasbro's initial release for some reason, yet retains a similar pose.

Notes: Distributed as a lucky-draw prize through the "Cybertron Keyword Present" campaign to celebrate the launch of Transformers 2010. The promotion required entrants to complete a partially filled name puzzle to reveal the new leader's full name (Rodimus Convoy). The lottery gave away 500 Battlechargers (only Runabout was depicted) and 50 "Convoy VS Megatron" VHS tapes.The campaign featured two separate entry methods that ran on completely different timelines:1. TV Magazine Promotion (Short Window): Featured as a print ad in the October 1986 issue of TV Magazine. It carried a fast, high-hype first-round deadline of October 31, 1986, to build mystery right before the new cartoon season debuted.2. Retail Leaflet Promotion (Extended Window): Packed as "Convoy is Dead!" leaflets inside boxed Transformers toys. Because retail store inventory lasted longer, this phase ran over a multi-month period from October 1986 until March 1987, allowing children who purchased toys during the Christmas season to call the automated phone hotline and mail entries until the final deadline on March 31, 1987.
